apply-canary-record._why: THE PRODUCER FOR A FILE THAT HAD ONLY CONSUMERS. Four documents (`audit.md` Step 4b/6a/7, `verify.md`, `staging.md`, `platform.md`) read `.claude/workforce/platform-local.md` and nothing wrote it; measured 2026-08-06 on this repository, a run recorded `INV-CANARY … PASS` in org-config.md and left no such file. DISPLAY is the default here as everywhere in wf-apply: the exact bytes are printed and nothing is written, which is what `not` asserts. `--measured-on` is pinned so the case is host-independent; the `claude --version` path was exercised by hand on 2026-08-06 and emitted `MEASURED-ON:  Claude Code 2.1.223` unaided. apply-canary-record-execute._why: `--execute` is the consent, same as every other pass in this script. Same tree and same arguments as apply-canary-record; the flag is the only difference and the verb changes from `would write` to `wrote`. `verified on disk:` is asserted because the confirmation RE-READS the file rather than echoing the string that was passed to write() — the defect being closed is a write that was believed and never made, so a report quoting its own input would reproduce it.

Only the two dead ones are named; calling the undecidable one dead would invite deleting a working registration, which is the failure wf-census's DEAD/UNDECIDABLE split exists for. `would apply` rather than `applied` is the whole difference between the two modes.

apply-deadhook-execute._why: --execute is the consent. Same tree as apply-deadhook; the only difference is the flag, and the verdict word changes from `would apply` to `applied`. Paired so a regression that makes display WRITE, or execute merely REPORT, fails one of them.

apply-emptyroot._why: wf-apply's plain (non-record-canary) DISPLAY path on a minimal root. The tree carries exactly one throwaway canary, .claude/agents/wf-canary-a.md, so PASS-STALE-CANARY has one named target; DISPLAY is the default, so the target and the --execute consent gate are printed and nothing is applied. Without a row the fixture tree was on disk and unasserted — a detector with no proof.

apply-stalecanary._why: THREE populations in one tree and only one is residue: a throwaway canary (no measures-fact:), a SHIPPED canary (carries measures-fact:, its job recurs per host and per harness version, never residue), and a real employee. Precision is a property of the three required conditions rather than a sample, and this asserts all three by naming what must NOT appear.

census-deadhook._why: Three registrations: one live, one whose script was deleted, and one `jq` resolved on PATH. The jq row must be UNDECIDABLE, never dead -- calling it dead invites deleting a working registration. --json is asserted separately for per-skill ownership, which is the input set sweep step 5 relocates from.

census-indented-mention._why: In markdown an indented line is a code block, so an indented sacred marker is documentation ABOUT the format and never a span opener. bin/baseline established this and measured 68 naive against 37 anchored -- 46% inflation -- and the other readers never got the ruling. The mention is REPORTED, never silently dropped: a number that shrank without explanation is its own defect. census-order._why: wf-census must name the tree BEFORE it counts anything in it. Commit 26ec383 appended the skills row above the title line, so every report opened with an orphan row above its header — a defect invisible in a diff because both lines are correct in isolation and only their ORDER is wrong. `want` asserts the title line is immediately followed by the skills row; `not` asserts the reverse (skills above a title) is absent, so a reversion fails this case.

checkrun-ambiguous._why: `ambiguous-markup` is the only ALWAYS-blocking row and had no fixture, while being produced by the masker rewritten in four separate rounds. An UNCLOSED FENCE is the canonical trigger; an unclosed HTML wrapper deliberately is not -- with lookahead it is ignored rather than quarantining the file, which is right once nothing executes: masking less risks a reporting miss, never a run.

checkrun-dead._why: A named check whose script is not on disk -- the analogue of dead wiring, and caught by RESOLUTION ALONE with no --run. A dead check reads as protection and enforces nothing.

checkrun-dead-also-in-prose._why: THE MECHANICAL VERDICT MUST WIN. The prose/fence token pass ran first and claimed the path, so a script named BOTH in a sentence and in a declared Check: produced only the non-blocking heuristic row -- exit 0, `0 blocking finding(s)`, which is exactly the 'printed clean' outcome this whole change exists to end. No fixture reached it because every dead-check fixture had a ## Verification containing nothing but the Check: line: fixtures written by the same hand as the extractor. The pre-fix code scored this silent, not correct: `printf` has no slash, so it stopped at segment one. Fixing the tokenizer without bringing the shell's command-prefix grammar along traded a silence for a false positive on a real tree.

checkrun-extensionless._why: The under-capture hole the SHARED resolver closes. `bash bin/verify` has no extension and no anchor, so the token pass correctly refuses to call it a file reference -- wf-census.resolve_hook_command unwraps the interpreter and answers it. checkrun-glob._why: `src/**/*.css` is this project's OWN canonical example. EXT_RX matched `.css`, so it resolved as a path and reported a blocking `dead` row -- every handbook copied from the shipped template failed. A glob is not a file. (The `want` clause was vacuous TWICE: `ran` matched 'qua-ran-tined', then `resolved` matched the always-printed summary '0 resolved'. checkrun-operator-dead._why: THE FALSIFICATION HALF of checkrun-operator, and the reason that case cannot pass vacuously. Identical shape, one token changed: `bin/gone.sh` is NOT in the tree. checkrun-orphan-negative._why: A Negative with no Check vanished from BOTH passes -- the falsify block returns early on no checks, and the resolver had already stripped the Negative line.

checkrun-placeholder._why: content-writer's actual shape: `... <draft>`, an argument the handbook never binds. The hook EXISTS here, so `resolved` passes and the finding is solely that the command cannot be executed as written -- which is why no one ever ran it.

checkrun-subshell._why: THE SILENT HALF of the same defect, found by writing the pair rather than by any report -- the audit that filed the false-dead row never saw this one. `cd "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR" && bash bin/real.sh` put `cd` in first position: no slash, so UNDECIDABLE, so the real script behind `&&` was never examined and the tool exited 0 having checked nothing. Under-reporting is the direction wf-census.load_ignore is explicitly written against, and it is the direction that hurts. `0 resolved` is asserted absent because that -- not a wrong row -- is what the failure looked like.

claudemd-absent._why: An absent CLAUDE.md is the GOAL STATE (SKILL.md - Directives, 2026-08-05), not a gap to fill. claudemd-evacuated._why: Every directive line reached a component — one a handbook, one the org charter — so the ledger is empty and CLAUDE.md may be deleted. DUPLICATED lines are counted as relocated because that is what duplicated MEANS; counting only the USER bucket made a two-rule fixture report one, understating the direction in the file.

Asserts the DEFECT IS NAMED, not merely a non-zero exit.

conform-ignored-corpus._why: TWO CHECKERS, ONE TREE, TWO DENOMINATORS -- the row a project audit filed alongside checkrun-operator, and the one with teeth: it was the sole reason wf-conform exited 1, which holds INV-VERIFY at NOT UPHELD and aborts any future sweep. `.censusignore` had three readers and one producer; wf-census and wf-apply honoured the declaration and wf-conform's sacred-block walk pruned a directory literally named `fixtures` and read nothing else. conform-invokes-spawner._why: TRUE POSITIVE GUARD for the routing exemption added 2026-08-05. A tier-3 IC that plainly invokes a spawning skill, with no escalation vocabulary anywhere, MUST still fail. The advisory row must fire and the exit code must stay 0 -- the contract post-dates every handbook under it, and failing them all reproduces the 9-false-failures run that taught this script 'a check that always fails stops being read'. The bin/check assertion can only see that the channel EXISTS; only this can see that it does not block.

conform-over-ceiling._why: TWO defects in one row, both measured. (1) CHANNEL: delegation-budget.md has always said over the ceiling is never a refusal, but the row was wired to the blocking channel, so 14 of them set a non-zero exit on odyssey-alive (2026-08-05) and INV-VERIFY read that exit as the org failing to verify. The advisory marker plus exit 0 plus no '✗ ' anywhere is what pins it to res.advise(). The run PERFORMS the split by relocation this run, so 'proposing' must NOT appear and the performed/relocated wording must. Paired with conform-under-ceiling: drop the advisory and this half fails; fire it unconditionally and that half fails.
want: the split is PERFORMED this run

conform-under-ceiling._why: The other half of conform-over-ceiling: a governed handbook of EXACTLY 150 body lines, sitting on the ceiling rather than under it, so the boundary is `<=` and an off-by-one would advise every at-ceiling handbook in the org. The ceiling row must be SILENT here — no advisory line, '0 advisory' in the summary, exit 0 — because a message that fires unconditionally would satisfy conform-over-ceiling's want-list on its own and prove nothing about detection. MUST pass. Paired with conform-removal-unstaged (the mark is missing) and conform-removal-unextracted (the extraction is missing) so each half of Step 6-S has a fixture that fails without it. `tree/` is asserted because the sweep unlinks the WHOLE directory — references/, scripts/, hooks/, datasets — and SKILL.md.orig is an undo for the least of that.

The only way to answer it was a hand grep — which on 2026-08-06 reported 37 sacred spans in skill-builder against the true 6, by matching indented examples and markers quoted mid-line inside the file that DOCUMENTS the marker format. Staged, marked, undo on disk, and one span unextracted: the target must be named with its file:line, not with the difference between two totals.

The finding must name the target and the step it is missing, never print a balanced-looking zero.

A line-local scope, or one that reads the prohibition-filtered text, reports this file.

Found on a real handbook 2026-08-04: the old 'Verification is not empty' assertion PASSED on it, because the wrong segment is also non-empty. Both scripts now match the heading line-anchored; this asserts wf-conform reports no failure on the file.

Those two guard the user's sacred text on a handful of paths, where a false clean is the failure. This one is advisory and fires on EVERY tool call, so an error message per call would itself be the runaway loop it exists to detect. The divergence is asserted here so it cannot later read as drift.

loopguard-corruptstate._why: The state file on disk is `{{{ this is not json`. FAIL-OPEN means the hook exits 0 and emits nothing, and stale-file tolerance means it REPLACES the garbage with a fresh window rather than carrying it. `after` is what makes those two claims separable: silent-and-recovered and silent-and-dead look the same on stdout, and a guard that leaves the corrupt file in place is silent forever afterwards.

loopguard-distinct._why: THE NEGATIVE HALF OF THE PAIR, and the one that fails if the detector ever stops discriminating. Window holds two DISTINCT prior calls; the third is distinct again, so the streak is 1 and the hook must say NOTHING -- a loop guard that nudges on ordinary distinct work is noise on every tool call and gets muted, which is the only failure mode that matters more than missing a loop. `after` asserts the state file was still WRITTEN while silent: silence and not-running produce identical stdout, and only the artifact tells them apart.

loopguard-nudge._why: THE POSITIVE HALF. Two identical Reads seeded, a third arrives, WF_LOOP_GUARD_NUDGE_AT defaults to 3 -- so rung 1 fires and rung 2 does not. The `want` list checks the NUDGE TEXT, not only that something was emitted: the nudge exists to force articulation (goal, why the last attempts failed, a different approach or ESCALATE), and a regression that reduced it to `repeated 3x` would still be a nudge and would still be useless. `not` pins that the advisory rung never halts while STOP_AT is 0.
want: wf-loop-guard: Read has now been called 3x with identical arguments

loopguard-stale._why: Identical seed to loopguard-nudge except `updated` is epoch 1.0, older than the 12h stale horizon this tree leaves at its default. A session id reused after half a day describes work that is over, so the window must reset and the third identical Read must be counted as the first. Without this the guard nudges about a loop nobody is in, on the first tool call of a fresh session.

loopguard-stop._why: Rung 2, which is OFF unless stop_at is set above 0 -- this fixture's tree sets stop_at=4 and seeds three identical Reads, so the fourth halts. Exit stays 0: the halt is carried by the `continue: false` payload, never by an exit code, because a PostToolUse exit 2 cannot undo the call that already ran. The stopReason must name the handoff to a different persona; a halt that tells the agent to resume itself returns it to the context that produced the loop.

Same tool, same arguments, same count of repeats -- and it must be silent, because an edit between two reads means the tree changed and the re-read is new information rather than a repeat. This is the whole discrimination between thrashing and legitimately repeated distinct work, and the two cases isolate it to that one record.

pincheck-badflags._why: A CONFLICT IS NAMED, NEVER SILENTLY RESOLVED. `--json` reports and writes nothing while `--execute` writes; a script that picked one would hand the caller a mode it did not ask for -- and in the losing direction it would write to a tree whose owner asked only to be told. Exit 2 marks it as a caller error, distinct from the 0 that every findings-bearing run returns, and `not` asserts nothing ran before the refusal.

Cargo is detected for dependabot coverage but not auto-pinned at launch, so its loose specs surface as UNPINNABLE naming the ecosystem and the reason instead of vanishing from a report that then reads clean. The precision assertion is in `not`: `[package]` carries `version = "0.1.0"` and `name = "fixture"`, which belong to the crate itself, and a scanner that regexes every `key = "value"` line would report `Cargo.toml: version 0.1.0` as an unpinned dependency -- a finding about a line it does not understand. `exact = "=1.2.3"` is already pinned by cargo's own grammar and must not be flagged either.
